newsitem.title: USA: Meridian and Cairn agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Meridian and Cairn agree to merge.

text.p: Meridian Resource Corp and Cairn Energy USA Inc said Monday they had entered into a definitive agreement for Meridian to acquire Cairn.
Terms call for the exchange of 1.08 shares of Meridian for each share of Cairn in a pooling-of-interests transaction that is expected to be tax-free to both companies, they said.
Meridian said it would issue about 18.9 million shares worth more than $234 million based on its July 3 closing stock price of 12-5/16.
The companies expect the merger to be accretive to 1997 per share cash flow and income, excluding one-time charges relating to expenses associated with the merger.

Meridian Chairman Joseph Reeves said, "The merger is the extension and expansion of high-potential exploration opportunities for two growth-minded companies who are leaders among the independent oil and gas companies in the development of 3-D seismic exploration projects."

Meridian is an independent oil and natural gas company engaged in the exploration for and development of oil and natural gas properties utilizing 3-D seismic technology, primarily in south Louisiana and southeast Texas.
Cairn explores for, develops and produces crude oil and natural gas, principally in the Outer Continental Shelf of the Gulf of Mexico.
